answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to earn influence through randomly assigned, peer-reviewed useful tasks that expire quickly. Like a lantern lighting only one path at a time, a task is assigned unpredictably, must be completed by that identity alone, and is checked by unrelated peers before any voting weight is granted. A thousand fake identities do not multiply power, because each must separately finish its own work, like hauling its own timber to build an oasis shelter. An attacker pays real effort per identity, linearly, while an honest agent pays once.
